question: One type of pulses is sold for ₹72 per kg at a 20% profit. Another type is sold for ₹60 per kg at a 25% profit. If these two varieties are mixed in the ratio of 2:1 (first variety to second variety) and the mixture is sold at ₹70 per kg, what is the overall profit or loss percentage?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

CP of first pulse = 72 × 100/120 = ₹60/kg

CP of second pulse = 60 × 100/125 = ₹48/kg

Net CP of mixture = (60 × 2 + 48 × 1) ÷ 3 = 168/3 = ₹56/kg

Overall Profit % = ((70 − 56) ÷ 56) × 100 = (14/56) × 100 = 25%

**∴ The correct answer is Profit of 25%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ SP of first variety = ₹72/kg, Profit = 20%

⇒ SP of second variety = ₹60/kg, Profit = 25%

⇒ Ratio of mixture (first : second) = 2 : 1

⇒ SP of mixture = ₹70/kg

**Formula Used:**

⇒ Cost Price (CP) = SP × 100 / (100 + Profit%)

⇒ Profit % = [(SP − CP) / CP] × 100

 
 

 

 
• 
 

 
 
 

 

 
 
 Type 1: 2 kg
 CP = ₹60/kg

 
 
 Type 2: 1 kg
 CP = ₹48/kg

 
 
 Mix CP: 3 kg
 Avg = ₹56/kg

 
 
 Mix SP
 ₹70/kg

 
 Profit = ₹14/kg (+25%)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the quantities of the two varieties be 2 kg and 1 kg respectively.

⇒ CP of 1st variety = 72 × 100 / (100 + 20) = 7200 / 120 = ₹60 per kg

⇒ Total CP for 2 kg of 1st variety = 60 × 2 = ₹120

⇒ CP of 2nd variety = 60 × 100 / (100 + 25) = 6000 / 125 = ₹48 per kg

⇒ Total CP for 1 kg of 2nd variety = 48 × 1 = ₹48

⇒ Total CP of 3 kg mixture = 120 + 48 = ₹168

⇒ Average CP of mixture = 168 ÷ 3 = ₹56 per kg

⇒ The SP of the mixture is given as ₹70 per kg

⇒ Overall Profit = SP − CP = 70 − 56 = ₹14 per kg

⇒ Profit Percentage = (Profit / CP) × 100 = (14 / 56) × 100 = (1 / 4) × 100 = 25%

**∴ The correct answer is Profit of 25%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Cost Price (CP)

The base price at which goods are purchased. It is the reference value for calculating profit or loss percentages. Formula: CP = SP × 100 / (100 + Profit%).

Mixtures & Alligation

A mathematical rule used to find the weighted average price of a mixture when two components with different prices are mixed in a specific ratio.

Profit & Loss Percentage

Profit and loss are always calculated over the overall Cost Price unless explicitly stated otherwise. Profit% = [(SP − CP) / CP] × 100.
